Percy Howard Newby (1918–1997), known as P. H. Newby, was a British novelist and broadcasting administrator. He was born on 25 June 1918 in Crowborough, Sussex, and his family moved around the British Midlands while he was growing up. He was educated at Hanley Castle Grammar School and trained as a teacher. During the Second World War he was seconded by the army to lecture in English literature at Cairo's Fuad 1st University. He won the inaugural Booker Prize in 1969 for *Something to Answer For*. Earlier, he received the Somerset Maugham Prize in 1948 for his debut novel. He joined the BBC in 1949 and worked there until 1978, rising to managing director of BBC Radio, and was made a CBE in 1972. He died on 6 September 1997 in Garsington, England.

Sources differ slightly on dates: one says the novel was published in 1968, while the Booker win is consistently given as 1969. The Booker Prize's own archive page is the primary reference for his prize.
